overview: A centriole is a single cylindrical structure; a centrosome is the larger organising complex made of a pair of centrioles plus surrounding material.
genZNote: Centriole is one Lego piece. Centrosome is the finished Lego set built from two of them.

aspects.label: Composition
aspects.valueA: A single cylindrical structure made of nine triplets of microtubules.
aspects.valueB: A pair of centrioles arranged at right angles, surrounded by pericentriolar material.

aspects.label: Function
aspects.valueA: Forms the base of cilia and flagella; contributes to spindle pole organisation.
aspects.valueB: Acts as the main microtubule-organising centre (MTOC) of animal cells.

aspects.label: Number per Cell
aspects.valueB: Usually one centrosome per animal cell (before duplication).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Plant cells generally lack centrioles/centrosomes but can still form a spindle during mitosis.
overlay.memoryTrick: Centriole = the small building block. Centrosome = the whole organising hub.
overlay.commonMisconception: Not all cells with a centrosome need centrioles to divide — higher plant cells manage spindle formation without either.
